definitions.explanation: The meat of sheep, as a category of food. A slightly technical or written word: menus and shops usually use ラム or マトン instead.

examples.japanese: {羊肉|ようにく}は{苦手|にがて}だ。
{北海道|ほっかいどう}では{羊肉|ようにく}をよく{食|た}べる。
examples.english: People eat a lot of mutton in Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{健康|けんこう}にいいと{言|い}われ、{羊肉|ようにく}の{消費量|しょうひりょう}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Consumption of mutton has been rising lately, as it is said to be good for your health.

notes:
From {羊|ひつじ} (sheep) + {肉|にく} (meat), following the same pattern as {牛肉|ぎゅうにく} and {豚肉|ぶたにく}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {羊肉|ようにく}{料理|りょうり}: mutton dishes
- {羊肉|ようにく}を{焼|や}く: to grill mutton
- {羊肉|ようにく}の{臭|にお}い: the smell of mutton

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ラム: lamb — meat from a young sheep, milder; the usual word on menus
- マトン: mutton — meat from an adult sheep, stronger in flavor
- ジンギスカン: Genghis Khan — the Hokkaido dish of grilled mutton and vegetables
